points.title: 早年成长
points.description: 约翰·多恩1572年出生于伦敦一个富裕的天主教家庭。他的父亲是富商，祖父是五金商人，曾因坚持天主教信仰而入狱。由于英国国教与天主教的冲突，多恩从小接受天主教教育，这深刻影响了他后来的宗教思想。在伦敦，他接受了良好的古典教育，展现出非凡的才华，12岁进入牛津大学，14岁进入剑桥大学，但因天主教徒身份无法获得学位。
points.descriptionEn: John Donne was born in London in 1572 to a wealthy Catholic family. His father was a successful ironmonger, and his grandfather had been imprisoned for his Catholic faith. Growing up during a time of religious conflict between Anglicanism and Catholicism, Donne received a Catholic education that profoundly influenced his later religious views. In London, he received excellent classical education and showed exceptional talent, entering Oxford University at age 12 and Cambridge at 14, but could not obtain degrees due to his Catholic faith.

points.title: 浪子生涯
points.description: 这一时期，多恩过着放荡不羁的生活，成为伦敦社交圈和文学界的活跃人物。他学习法律，但并未真正执业。1596-1597年，他随埃塞克斯伯爵远征加的斯，随后参加了亚速尔群岛远征。1598年，他秘密与安妮·莫尔结婚，此举激怒了她的叔叔，导致多恩被短暂监禁。这段经历使他失去了社会地位，但也促使他开始反思生活。在此期间，他创作了大量爱情诗歌，展现了其独特的智性风格和奇特的比喻。
points.descriptionEn: During this period, Donne lived a rakish life, becoming an active figure in London's social and literary circles. He studied law but never practiced it. From 1596-1597, he accompanied the Earl of Essex on expeditions to Cadiz and the Azores. In 1598, he secretly married Anne More, which angered her uncle and resulted in Donne's brief imprisonment. This experience cost him social position but prompted him to begin reflecting on life. During this time, he wrote numerous love poems, showcasing his distinctive intellectual style and unusual metaphors.

points.title: 宗教转变
points.description: 1615年，多恩放弃天主教信仰，加入英国国教并被任命为牧师。这一转变源于他对宗教的深刻思考和对家庭责任的考量。1615-1627年间，他迅速晋升，先后成为王室牧师、伦敦圣保罗大教堂教长。这一时期，他创作了大量布道文和宗教诗歌，如《神圣十四行诗》，将玄学风格与宗教主题完美结合。他的布道文以其深刻的神学见解和雄辩的口才著称，吸引了大量听众，包括国王詹姆斯一世和查理一世。
points.descriptionEn: In 1615, Donne renounced his Catholic faith, joined the Church of England, and was ordained as a priest. This conversion stemmed from his deep religious reflections and considerations of family responsibility. From 1615-1627, he rose rapidly through the ranks, becoming Royal Chaplain and Dean of St. Paul's Cathedral. During this period, he wrote numerous sermons and religious poems, such as 'Holy Sonnets,' perfectly combining metaphysical style with religious themes. His sermons were renowned for their profound theological insights and eloquent delivery, attracting large audiences including King James I and Charles I.

points.title: 晚年创作
points.description: 晚年多恩健康状况恶化，但仍坚持创作。1627年，他被任命为伦敦圣保罗大教堂教长，这是他职业生涯的最高峰。在生命的最后几年，他创作了著名的《疾病中的冥想》，这是一组面对死亡的神学思考。这些作品展现了他对生命、死亡和信仰的深刻思考，语言更加凝练，思想更加成熟。1631年3月31日，多恩在伦敦逝世，临终前发表了著名的'告别布道'，被视为英国文学史上的经典之作。
points.descriptionEn: In his later years, Donne's health deteriorated but he continued to write. In 1627, he was appointed Dean of St. Paul's Cathedral in London, the pinnacle of his career. In his final years, he wrote his famous 'Devotions upon Emergent Occasions,' a collection of theological meditations facing death. These works demonstrate his profound reflections on life, death, and faith, with more concise language and mature thought. Donne died in London on March 31, 1631, delivering his famous 'Death's Duel' sermon on his deathbed, considered a masterpiece in English literary history.

supporter.zh: 约翰·多恩被玄学派诗歌的奠基人，其作品展现了非凡的智性深度和创造力。他的诗歌将哲学思考与情感体验完美融合，开创了独特的玄学风格。作为牧师，他的布道文充满神学洞见和人文关怀，影响了后世宗教思想。多恩的作品跨越了世俗与神圣的界限，展现了人类经验的复杂性，对后世文学和宗教思想产生了深远影响。
supporter.en: John Donne is celebrated as the founder of metaphysical poetry, whose works demonstrate extraordinary intellectual depth and creativity. His poetry perfectly merges philosophical thought with emotional experience, pioneering a distinctive metaphysical style. As a priest, his sermons are filled with theological insights and human compassion, influencing later religious thought. Donne's works transcend the boundaries between secular and sacred, revealing the complexity of human experience and exerting profound influence on later literature and religious thought.

critic.zh: 批评者认为多恩的诗歌过于晦涩难懂，充满了牵强附会的比喻和复杂的智力游戏。他的宗教转变被视为政治机会主义，而非真正的信仰转变。此外，多恩的诗歌中常表现出对女性的矛盾态度，既有崇拜又有控制欲。他的布道文也被批评为过于华丽，有时牺牲了神学的清晰性。这些批评反映了多恩作品中的时代局限和个人矛盾。
critic.en: Critics argue that Donne's poetry is overly obscure, filled with far-fetched conceits and complex intellectual games. His religious conversion is viewed as political opportunism rather than genuine spiritual transformation. Additionally, Donne's poetry often shows contradictory attitudes toward women, exhibiting both admiration and control. His sermons have also been criticized as overly ornate, sometimes sacrificing theological clarity. These criticisms reflect the limitations of his era and personal contradictions in his work.

objective.zh: 在历史学和流行文化中，约翰·多恩被定义为英国文学史上最具创新精神的诗人之一。他的'没有人是孤岛'的比喻已成为西方文化中的经典表达，象征着人类相互联系的本质。多恩的作品跨越了文艺复兴和巴洛克时期，展现了时代过渡期的思想特征。他的诗歌和布道文对17世纪英国文学产生了深远影响，并启发了后来的T.S.艾略特等现代主义诗人。在当代，多恩被视为连接中世纪与现代思想的重要桥梁。
objective.en: In historical and popular culture, John Donne is defined as one of the most innovative poets in English literary history. His metaphor 'No man is an island' has become a classic expression in Western culture, symbolizing the interconnected nature of humanity. Donne's works span the Renaissance and Baroque periods, reflecting the intellectual characteristics of a transitional era. His poetry and sermons profoundly influenced 17th-century English literature and inspired later modernist poets like T.S. Eliot. Today, Donne is regarded as an important bridge connecting medieval and modern thought.

self.zh: 没有人是孤岛，任何人的死亡都使我有所缺损，因为我与人类难解难分。
self.en: No man is an island, entire of itself; every man is a piece of the continent, a part of the main.

others.zh: 多恩是英国文学中最具原创性和智性深度的诗人之一，他的作品将哲学思考与情感体验完美融合，开创了独特的玄学风格。
others.en: Donne is one of the most original and intellectually profound poets in English literature, whose works perfectly merge philosophical thought with emotional experience, pioneering a distinctive metaphysical style.
